paper.title: Achieving Near Instance-Optimality and Minimax-Optimality in Stochastic and Adversarial Linear Bandits Simultaneously

settings.name_in_paper: corrupted setting (linear bandit, finite action set)
unmapped: corruption c_t chosen before seeing x_t; C = sum_t max_x |<x,c_t>|
settings.definition_quote: The corrupted setting is a generalization of the stochastic setting, where in addition to a fixed vector $\theta$, the environment also decides a corruption vector $c_t \in \mathbb{R}^d$ for each round (before seeing $x_t$) so that $\ell_t = \theta + c_t$. We define the total amount of corruption as $C=\sum_t\max_{x\in\calX}|\inner{x, c_t}|$.

settings.name_in_paper: stochastic setting (linear bandit, finite action set)
settings.definition_quote: In the stochastic setting, $\ell_t$ is fixed to some unknown vector $\theta\in\mathbb{R}^d$. We assume that there exists a unique optimal arm $x^*\in\calX$
the environment also decides a corruption vector $c_t \in \mathbb{R}^d$ for each round (before seeing $x_t$) so that $\ell_t = \theta + c_t$.

settings.name_in_paper: adversarial setting (linear bandit, finite action set)
unmapped: observations include zero-mean noise; <x,l_t> and y_t in [-1,1]
settings.definition_quote: Finally, in the adversarial setting, $\ell_t$ can be chosen arbitrarily (possibly dependent on the learner's algorithm and her previously chosen actions). ... $\Reg(T)=\max_{x\in\calX}\sum_{t=1}^T\inner{x_t-x,\ell_t}$.

settings.name_in_paper: adversarial environment for lower bound (lower bound)
unmapped: hard environment is piecewise stochastic with a single switch of theta
settings.definition_quote: We fix a stochastic linear bandit instance ... Assume that $\|x\|\leq 1$ for all $x\in\calX$ and $\|\theta\|\leq \frac{1}{4}$. ... We now define the second environment as follows: in intervals $1,\ldots, i-1$, the losses are generated according to $\theta$, but in intervals $i,\ldots, S$, the losses are generated according to $\theta'$.

symbols.c_X_theta: value of the instance-optimal lower-bound optimisation problem c(X, theta)
symbols.M_star: problem-dependent constant depending only on X and theta

source.label: thm: sto-alg-guarantee
source.quote: In the corrupted setting, \pref{alg:REOLB} guarantees that with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\Reg(T) = \order(c(\calX, \theta)\log T\log\frac{T|\calX|}{\delta}+M^*\log^\frac{3}{2}\frac{1}{\delta} + C + d\sqrt{\frac{C}{\Delta_{\min}}} \log\frac{C|\calX|}{\Delta_{\min}\delta})$, where $M^*$ is some constant that depends on $\calX$ and $\theta$ only.

results.notes: Regret defined via gaps (pseudo-regret realized path), bound with high probability. K=|X|. Algorithm does not need C or T. The paper does not define c(X,theta) as a canonical C_lin exactly (constraint ||x||^2 <= Delta_x^2/2), so a custom symbol is used. Stochastic case is C=0.

source.label: thm: regret_part1-main
source.quote: In the corrupted setting, \pref{alg:REOLB} guarantees that with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\Reg(T)\leq \order(d\sqrt{T}\log(T|\calX|/\delta)+C)$.

source.label: thm: no-M-dependency
source.quote: \pref{alg:REOLB} guarantees that with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\Reg(T) = \order\left(\frac{d^2}{\Delta_{\min}}\log^2\left(\frac{T|\calX|}{\Delta_{\min}\delta}\right)+C \right)$.

results.notes: Conditions C<=T and T>=d used in proof (AM-GM step). Setting is corrupted (statement implicit).

symbols.c_X_theta: value of the instance-optimal lower-bound optimisation problem c(X, theta)
symbols.M_star: problem-dependent constant depending only on X and theta
symbols.C_1: regret coefficient of the black-box adversarial algorithm A (Assumption 1), C_1 >= 2^15 d log(T|X|/delta)
symbols.L_0: minimum time after which A's guarantee (Assumption 1) holds

tuning: black-box A satisfies Assumption 1 with C_2 >= 20

source.label: thm: sto-and-corrupt
source.quote: \pref{alg: BOBW} guarantees that with probability at least $1-\delta$, in the stochastic setting ($C=0$), $\Reg(T)$ is at most $\order(c(\calX,\theta)\log T\log\frac{T|\calX|}{\delta}+\frac{C_1\sqrt{\log T}}{\Delta_{\min}}+M^*\log^{\frac{3}{2}}\frac{1}{\delta} + \sqrt{C_1L_0})$

symbols.C_1: regret coefficient of the black-box adversarial algorithm A (Assumption 1)
symbols.L_0: minimum time after which A's guarantee holds

tuning: black-box A satisfies Assumption 1 with C_2 >= 20

source.label: thm: sto-and-corrupt
source.quote: and in the corrupted setting ($C>0$), $\Reg(T)$ is at most $\order\left(\frac{C_1\log T}{\Delta_{\min}}+C+\sqrt{C_1L_0}\right)$.

results.notes: Corrupted part of Theorem 6, generic black-box.

tuning: A = variant of GeometricHedge.P with John's exploration

source.label: thm: sto-and-corrupt
source.quote: In the case when $\calA$ is the variant of GeometricHedge.P, the last bound is $\order\left(\frac{d\log(T|\calX|/\delta)\log T}{\Delta_{\min}}+C\right)$.

results.notes: Instantiation of corrupted bound with GeometricHedge.P black box.

symbols.C_1: regret coefficient of the black-box adversarial algorithm A (Assumption 1)
symbols.L_0: minimum time after which A's guarantee holds

tuning: black-box A satisfies Assumption 1 with C_2 >= 20

source.label: thm: fully adversarial
source.quote: In the adversarial setting, \pref{alg: BOBW} guarantees that with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\Reg(T)$ is at most $\order\left(\sqrt{C_1 T\log T}+\sqrt{C_1L_0}\right)$.

results.notes: With GeometricHedge.P, C_1 = Theta(d log(T/delta')), giving roughly O(sqrt(dT) log(...)) (paper text). Also holds in stochastic setting.

conditions: algorithm guarantees stochastic pseudo-regret at most c_reg*c(X,theta)*(1-gamma)/log(4/Delta_min)*(log T)^2 with c_reg = gamma/256 for all sufficiently large T

source.label: thm: lower bound
source.quote: For any $\gamma \in(0,1)$, if an algorithm guarantees a pseudo regret bound of $c_{\reg}\cdot c(\calX,\theta)\frac{1-\gamma}{\log \frac{4}{\Delta_{\min}}}(\log T)^2$ for constant $c_{\reg}=\frac{\gamma}{256}$ in stochastic environments for all sufficiently large $T$, then there exists an adversarial environment such that with probability at least $\frac{1}{4} T^{-\frac{1}{4}\gamma}$, the regret of the same algorithm is at least $\frac{1}{6}T^{\gamma}\Delta_{\min}$.

results.notes: Holds with small probability T^{-gamma/4}/4; recorded as realized regret. Shows extra log T factor is necessary for algorithms also robust w.h.p. in adversarial settings.

_verify.summary: The extraction is accurate. All main theorems (1, 2, 6, 7, 19, 27) are recorded with the right expressions, sides, probability types and settings, and I found no errors that need correcting. The only debatable choices are small: the lower-bound environment is coded as oblivious adversarial when it is in fact a single-switch stochastic environment, and the vanishing-probability lower bound carries the label high_probability.
